articleTitle: Transmission Line Electric Field (EF) Parameters Control in Space and on Man's Body
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Problems concerning the development of EF intensity meters, devices for measuring induced currents on man's body and dose-meters for estimating the resulting effect of EF with different intensity on man are considered.

articleTitle: Analysis of Quasi-Peak Radio Interference Voltage Caused by Random Modulated Switching Stress
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: It is shown that instability of electric duties of apparatus operation leads to change of switching stress parameters causing amplitude-impulse (AI) and phase-impulse (PhI) modulation which are usually of random character. An analysis of quasi-peak radio interference voltage caused by commutation is made, account being taken of random AI and PhI. The calculation method depends on ratio of switching stress frequencies and radio interference meter band. It is based on the solution of the differential equation of the quasi-peak detector. The results received allow to take into account modulation phenomenon while calculating switching interferences on the stage of apparatus design and may be used for perfection of test methods of radio-electronic apparatus and electronic vacuum apparatus as interference sources.

articleTitle: Optimization of a Random Search for an RF Channel Plan Which Provides for a Minimum Frequency Band
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The Report consideres a problem of drawing up an RF channel plan for an aggregate of diversity-spaced radio facilities. The minimization of a frequency hand is effected by means of a random search which realizes the ideas of local optimization and adaptation. It is shown that the time of solution of the problem is substantially reduced if, in the algorithm structure, account is taken of the priori information and of information obtained in the process of searching.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Effects in the Ionosphere and the Magnetosphere from Seismo-Acoustic Actions
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The large-scale acoustic wave from the explosions with hundreds tons TNT can be effectively used for the investigation of the electromagnetic processes in the ionosphere and the magnetosphere. In the magnetic tube conjugated with the explosion epicenter, the wide spectrum of the electrostatic and whistler oscillations arise and the sharp electromagnetic impulse is exited. This impulse oscillates between ionospheres and slowly drifts across the geomagnetic field.

articleTitle: Spatial Diffraction Field Characteristics of Sector Screens Optimized for Increasing the Effectivness of Disturbing Field Suppression
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Calculation and analythis of spatial sizes and shapes of suppression regions created by optimized sector-type screens near focal points are presented. Spatial characteristics of created suppression regions are of great importance for direct choice of the most effective variants of screens under concrete real conditions of interfering field suppression. Sizes and configurations of screening region dependences of screen type, sizes and displacement are exposed.

articleTitle: Difraction Isolation of the Edge
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The experimental study of SHF antenna isolation has been performed by of diffraction screens by chanellising effect of the conducting semi-plane edge. Tranverse diffraction elements have shown to increase isolation by polarisation with H vector parallel to the semi-plane do not give interference attenuation. The posibillity of field attenuation at the conducting edge has been proved by means of a longitudinal screen with E parallel to the semi-plane. The directing effect of the conducting edge has been first found to depend on its irregularities. On this basis the posibillity of antenna isolation was stated by selection of certain dispersion of irregularitties.

articleTitle: Radio Interference Meter Modelling by a Computer
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: It is shown that if one wants to analyse radio interferences created by an apparatus in the automatic design systems as well as to make the process of interference measurements automatic it is necessary to develop radio interference meter models. A method of radio interference meter modelling oriented on the computer use is considered. The meter model meets the scheme of direct amplification receiver and consists of models of a band filter, a set of detectors, an indicator and matching devices. Basic requirements to the models of the units are considered with the purpose of securing main selectivity characteristics and impulse parameters of the radio interference meter. A radio interference meter for frequency range 0,15 - 30 MHz is given as an example.

articleTitle: Transmission of Colour Signal Components
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The paper deals with two metods of transmission of colour signal components: - transmission of analog components with compression and time - multiplexing - transmission of digital components with time - multiplexing. Technical parameters of these two metods were discussed and optimum values of the parameters were determined. Comparison "between these two metods with regard to reproduced picture quality and frequency spectrum utilization was carried out, too.

articleTitle: Questions of Optimization of Electromagnetic Interference Parameters Measurements
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Questiona are treated, which concern optimization of procedures of classification and measurement of electromagnetic interference that have a preliminary unknown amplitude-time and spectral structure. An optimum structure of a measuring apparatus in a guasaian approximation is synthesized.

articleTitle: UHF Tropospheric Propagation in Extreme Climate Conditions
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The paper presente investigation results of statistical characteristics of fast and low troposcatter signal fluctuations at intervals of radiorelay line, located in the conditions of the sharp continental climate on high latitudes. A detailed analysis of radiometeorological situations causing abnormal high increases of signal levels is presented, and climate conditions forming low signal levels are exposed.

articleTitle: Parameters of Short Time Voltage Transients in Shipboard Electrical Systems
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Short time voltage transients are due to load switchings and ground faults in shipboard electrical systems. Calculations of transients may be based on the proposed equivalent circuits. Results of calculations and measurements of pulse voltages in shipboard electrical systems (380 V, 50 Hz) led to the conclusion that shipboard electronic equipments must be protected from impulses at peak voltages up to 600 V and for some cases to 1200 V.

articleTitle: An Active Antenna for Time Domain Electric Field Strength Investigation
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Assuming nondistorted envelope response criterion of the antenna network, the formula of antenna factor and required active unit impedance have been derivated. Some technical parameters data of the constructed antenna have been discussed there, too, and also, some results of the electric field strength investigation achieved in the neighborhood of the electromechanical interrupter suplying line has been brought forward.

articleTitle: The Influence of Meteorology of the GOBI on the VHF and UHF Signal Levels
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The influences of meteorology of the desert region Gobi of Mongolia on the average field level are examined. Camparisons of the seasonal variation and variation during the day of recieved signal with the corresponding variation of the air refractive index and its gradient are given. Correlation coefficient between the average signal attenuation and the air refractive index is determined for different season of the year.

articleTitle: Signal Stability and Interference Immunity of a Radio System on Closed Land Paths
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The paper presents the results of experimental investigation of fine spatial structure of diffraction field and its effect on signal characteristics for the aim of communication and EMC. It s found that the signal time fluctuations are considerably dependent on the features of spatial picture of the field in the shadow zone of diffraction obstacles. It is shown that the choice of receive antenna location on spatial pattern enables one to improve communication condition and reduce interference.

articleTitle: Interference Immunity of Synchronous CDMA Cellular Mobile System
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The problem of interference immunity of synchronous CDMA cellular mobile system is considered, it is shown in the report, that in calculation of SIR one should take into account the following: under the condition of multipath effect the orthogonality of code channels is disturbed and the level of interference grows at the expense of cross-correlation.

articleTitle: Calculation of Overhead Line Electromagnetic Field Integrals for Multilayer Structure and High-Resistivity Ground
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: A method of computation of Carson-type electromagnetic field integrals of a multiconductor overhead power transmission line for the case of multilayer structure and high-resistivity ground is described. Nodal points are distributed non-uniformly over the integration interval taking into account the form of the integrand. When forming the matrix of multiconductor line integrals, the nucleus of the integrals, as well as all identical integrals are found by a single computation. The calculation error is within 10<inf>-3</inf>%. The algorithm is coded in PL/1 language of the IBM/360 system. A minor modification makes the program applicable for evaluating integrals of arbitrary complex variable functions, including high-oscillation functions.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Precursor Emission and Possible Source Mechanisms
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The registration of abnormal electromagnetic emission in the epicenter region of the earthquake and at a distance are discussed. The model of near surface sources location is submited. It is emphasised that the electromagnetic effects due to the earthquakes in the inviroment could be compared with the effects of aurora or magnetic storm.

articleTitle: The Measurement of Radio Interference Meters Amplitude Relationship by Pulse Repetition Rate Switching
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The measurement of amplitude relationship directly according to its definition has metrological disadvantage because it requires high accuracy of the spectrum amplitude absolute value. The method of amplitude relationship measurement with switching to the repetition rate exeeding the RI meter bandwidth reduced the measurement to the pulse repetition rate and difference attenuation measurements. At low tuning frequency videopulses are applied and at high frequency - radiopulses.

articleTitle: Problems of tv Transmitters EMC
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Results of studies aimed at the development of protection ratios for D,K/SECAM television in the presence of interference from other transmitting systems in broadcasting services are given. Protection ratio curves are first obtained, which correspond to different reception quality. The results are compared with other similar studies. The proposals are provided to establish unified protection ratio curves in accordance with current CCIR activities on the revision of Report 306.

articleTitle: Cellular Communications Systems
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Prospects for the future development of cellular communications systems are discribed· The large-scale inculcation of cellular digital radiotelephone is shown to mark the appearance of new mass radio-telecommunioations systems including radio and wire communications switching and computer technology· Some results of the use of cellular mobile communications systems (CMCS) are given and it is shown that EMC of the real CMCSs is worse than it has been assumed· The reasons of EMC deterioration are given. The ways of improvement of EMC with the help of pseudo-noise signals (PNS) are discussed. Also shown is the potential of CMCS with PNS.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Conditions of Safe Dose Influence Caused by Power Frequency Electrical Fields on SHV Substation Personnel
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: In the report the results of dosimetric control of personnel exposure to electric field in operational areas of Class 300 and 750kV substations and medical-physiological examination of the personnel are presented. Basing on the analysis of the data obtained and those available in literature an analytical expression for the conditions of dose influence caused by power frequency electrical field within the coordinates "power frequency electrical field intensity in the free zone - exposure time in the operational zone" <tex>${\text T}= \frac{50}{E} - {2}$</tex> which allows the normalization of high-voltage installations maintanance time, is proposed.

articleTitle: Signal Phase Fluctuations in Mobile Radio Antenna
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The paper presents experimental measurement results of variations in signal phase difference from the outpute of two spased antennas in urban mobile radio. Autocorrelation intervale of signal phase difference have been determined by longitudinal and traverse antenna spacing in the vehicle. Estimetes of conditions of synphase signal superposition are givon.

articleTitle: Bees Etological Anomalies in SHV Transmission Line Areas
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Peculiarities of honey bees ontogeny, physiology and ecology in 0.5 - 80kV/m electrical fields (EF) have been investigated in laboratory tests and field experiments. Biological effect of SHV transmission line EF on the organism (individual) and micropopulation (bee colony) levels has been determined.

articleTitle: Account of Signal Distortions in Interconnections when Designing Superrapid-Acting Digital Units of Radio-Electronic Apparatus
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The paper deals with one of the most important problems of intra-apparatus EMC: account of signal distortions in interconnections. It is proposed to analyse the signal distortion influence in communication lines upon functioning of digital units of radio-electronic apparatus and electronic-vacuum apparatus at the stage of their design by means of machine calculations of full-scale models including the models of elemental base and the models of the interconnections used. Main calculation relations are given for determination of parameters of the models used. Software of the proposed analysis is described. A number of results are given and analysed illustrating the stages of the solution of the problem under discussion.

articleTitle: The Use of Capacitor with Ring Electrodes for Dipole low Frequency Antennas Calibration
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The use of capacitor with ring electrodes as a sourse of standard electric field for dipole antennas calibration used at frequencies less than 100 kHz is considered. On the basis of the electric field estimation the optimum relationship is chosen between the radius of ring electrodes and the distance between them for obtaining uniform field along the axis connecting electrodes centres. It is shown that the capacitor with ring eletrodes has advantages as compared with a flat capacitor, because the antenna and ring electrodes interaction essentially less than that of the antenna and solid electrodes, what makes the minimisation of the standard field sourse dimensions possible so important for practical use.

articleTitle: Necessary and Sufficient Conditions for the Existence of Electromagnetic Compatibility of a Radioelectronic Device and a Radioelectronic Complex
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Statements (theorems) that provide the necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of EMC of a radioelectronic device and a radioelectronic complex are formulated and proved true. The aggregate mechanism of the theory of complex systems, concepts from linear algebra and a model, worked out by the author are used.

articleTitle: Modelling of Connectors for Computer Analysis of Interferences in Inter-Connectors of Quick-Operating Apparatus
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: It is shown that in modern digital apparatus account of nonuniformities caused by communication lines interconnections is necessary. An analysis of interferences in connectors is given with their analytical description made by means of approximation of the time function describing the signal reflected from the nonuniformity with the help of exponential polinomials. A method of connector model development on the basis of synthesis in the time region with the use of experimental data is considered. Models of connectors of specific types developed by this method are proposed. The models received may be used while designing of communication lines of quick-operating digital apparatus with the help of computer.

articleTitle: Principles of Systems' Elements Assembling According to Permissible Level of EM or Thermal Field
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Constructive estimation of permissible density of assembling is suggested. The estimation is performed on the basis of EM, thermal or any other compatibility of the system elements. It is shown that neglecting the problem of elements compatibility frequently causes unreliable operation of various equipment. The generalized geometric model of an element, writ or functionally completed part of a system is suggested. This model makes it possible to ensure the optimally dense assembling of system elments with due regard to their EM or any other compatibility.

articleTitle: Nonsinusoidal Signals Emission by Elementary Dipoles
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: In the paper nonsinusoidal signal emission is investigated when the elementary antennas are excited by the signal source with an electromotive force e(t) and intrinsic impedance R.

articleTitle: The Effect of Frequency Response Non-Similarity in Receiving Channels of a Two-Channel Canceller on Interference Suppression Effectiveness
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The non-similarity efect of frequency and phase responses of receiving channels of a two-channel canceller on the effectiveness of interference suppression has been analysed, the analysis was carried out under the conditions that: - channel frequency responses differ insignificantly; - frequency bands occupied by signal and interference are equal; - noise energy spectrum is uniform and limited in a bandwidth. Two types of filters (a Butterworth filter and a Chebyshev filter) used in receiving channels are considered. Interference suppression is evaluated by signal to noise power ratio at the canceller output. It is shown that with the improvement in discrimination of filters usee in the channels and with higher non-uniformity of their frequency responses, the requirement for similarity of frequency responses becomes more stringent. Examples of calculating the allowable differences in pass-bands and receiving channel group delays are given.

articleTitle: Slot-Type Diffraction Screens for Interfering Field Suppression
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Optimization for slot screen parameters is performed for increasing the effectiveness of interfering field suppression. In case of screens with arbitrary number of slots engineering method is proposed to find optimal values of their parameters providing effective suppresion of interfering wave in a fixed direction. With a view to make it computable and to increase accuracy of calculation this method has been programmed and algorithm for solving of optimizational equations has been worked out. The precisive values of optimal screen parameters have been defined by means of algorithm and necessary for analythis spatial sizes and shape of suppression regions created near the focal points have been determined.

articleTitle: A Mathematical Model of the Effect of Quasi-Harmonic Interference on a Radio-Telephone Frequency-Modulation Receiver
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The Report lists the results of analysis of receiver susceptibility to quasi-harmonic interference. Analytical results are confirmed by experimental investigations. It is pointed out that the susceptibility of the receivers in question to out-of-channel interference is affected mainly by local-oscillator noise. A mathematical model is given of the effect of those interferences on a receiver, which get into its main receiving-channel and outside its limits.

articleTitle: Reflector Repeaters with the Improved Noise Immunity
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: A method for determining reflector repeaters configuration for relay lines that minimizes the sidelobe radiation power in one or several angular sectors is considered. The problem is solved by both analytical (for power reduction on one plane) and programming methods (for two planes of reduction).

articleTitle: Efficient Utilization of Radio-Frequency Spectrum Resource by Land Mobile Service
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The potentialities of efficient utilization of RF spectrum resource for establishing land mobile networks are considered. These potentialities are realizable within an idealized regular network where information is transmitted by the most efficient modulation techniques taking into account the information properties of the messages transmitted. Transmitters in this idealized network are free of out-of-band and spurious emissions and receivers are characterized by perfect selectivity characteristics.

articleTitle: Numerical Methods for the Analysis of Multifrequency and Stochastic Oscillations
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The report considers the conditions of arising qualitative changes (bifurcations) in the dynamics of nonlinear circuits, these bifurcations resulting in the transformation of spectral and some other characteristics of a signal. The significance of these changes for the EMC is analyzed, numerical algorithms are discussed allowing to identify bifurcational phenomena occurring as the system parameters change. The packet of applied programs realizing these algorithms is described.

articleTitle: An Algorithm of a Frequency Band Minimization by Means of a Predetermined Matrix of Frequency Tunings-Away on the Basis of Statistical Local Optimization
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Data are given of the investigation of results of repeated local optimization in a problem of minimization of a frequency band occupied by a group consisting of N uniform simultaneously operating radio facilities. Expedience of a statistical approach to the results of local optimization is shown, and statistical regularities are investigated. On the basis of the investigation, an adaptive algorithm of approximate minimization of a frequency band is proposed. This adaptive algorithm guarantees obtaining a good frequency-assignment plan for a group of several dozens of radio facilities which are located on a confined territory.

articleTitle: Optimization of Parameters for an Extrapolator of Signals with an Essentally Non-Uniform Spectrum Used in Interference Pulse Cancellers
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: A method for suppressing interfering pulses has been investigated; it allows interfered areas of a signal to be recovered by means of an extrapolator based on a reactive one-port. This extrapolator is advantageous when signal spectrum is highly non-uniform. Extrapolator's elements are chosen so that the extrapolator has maximum resistance at frequecies corresponding to spectrum maximums. Non-uniform spectrum is typical for the systems where messages are transmitted on subcarriers (VHF-FM stereo broadcasting, TV broadcasting etc.). The extrapolation accuracy of the method proposed is given. Optimum parameters of a reactive one-port are determined. The efficiency of this method is compared with that of other known techniques used for an interfering pulse suppression.

articleTitle: Co-Located F M Broadcasting Antenna Systems
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Problems are discussed related to the designing and use of co-located antenna systems for FM broadcasting. Antenna systems are intended for frequency ranges /66 - 74/ MHz and /100 - 108/ MHz. The results of researches in two aspects are analized: - influence of the antenna mast and the respective antenna system on the gain pattern of the other antenna system; - the mutual influence of the transmitters with regard to the transfer of electromagnetic power between the antenna systems.

articleTitle: Noise Imitator
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The paper describes a computer controlled imitator for electromagnetic disturbances on low voltage power lines designed for laboratory testing of EMC of electronic devices

articleTitle: The Principles of Development of Urban Radiotelephone System with Cellular Structure
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: This report considers the principles of development of urban radio-telephone network with cellular structure and directional antennas. The methods of calculation of mutual interference in the system, working in the UHF range is suggested. The calculation of interference level when using directional antennas of a horn type is made.

articleTitle: Prediction Method of Surveillance Radars Mutual Pulse Interference
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The electromagnetic compatibility and electromagnetic environment definitions are given. The mechanism of mutual pulse interference in a radar network, the parameters being the measure of these interference and the permissible distance between radars beyond which the mutual interferences are not effective are described. An example of mutual pulse interference calculation for the network of four "Avia C" air route surveillance radars is given.

articleTitle: The Digital Integrated Circuits Susceptibility to Influence of LEMP and NEMP
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: This paper is primary concerned with the analysis of some types digital IC Circuits susceptibility to disturbances which are caused by LEMP and NEMP. The electronic equipments were tested is the following manner : - a generated transients overvoltages were put to the circuits - electric and magnetic firlds impining directly to the circuits. Finally, some results about the circuits susceptibility were presented.

articleTitle: Microwave Link Antennas with Increased Interference Immunity
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The results of development of microwave offset antennas to be used in the range of 3.2 ... 13, 25 GHz are presented. Described antennas provide for high matching with feeding waveguide and increased interference immunity.

articleTitle: Statistical Quality Researches of the Data Transmission Link in a Land Mobile Radio Communication
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The communication quality evaluation method by a communication probability defined as a given information marks number in fixed time and error rate transmission probability has been proposed. The experimental results of communication quality measurements in the VHF low power stations link using data transmission sets with the acceptation feedback have been also presented. The qualities of stationary and quastmobile links of the same distances have been compared and the indispensable signal level for the same communication quality keeping has been appointed. The operational range appointing method, with communication quality and signal level along the radio link distribution requirements, has been given, too.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Transients in Public Low Voltage Power Installations
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Measurements of the electric field strength from lightning and the related induced voltage transients in low voltage power (l.v.p.) installations have been performed in two different structures. The small dipole antenna theory has been used to estimate the ”effective equivalent antenna height" of the investigated l.v.p. installations. The validity of the small dipole antenna model has been confirmed by calculating the induced voltage transients in the installations, using the measured electric field strength oscillograms, and comparing the calculated waveforms with the measured voltage transients.

articleTitle: HF Radio Noise above the Ionospher Observed on ISS-B
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The HF electro-magnetic environment at the satellite height was observed by the fixed-frequency receivers on Ionosphere Sounding Satellite (ISS-b). The statistical characteristics of various kinds of radio noises including the solar radio noise, the cosmic radio noise, the noise from lightning discharges and man-made radio noises emitted from transmitters on the ground were measured and analized.

articleTitle: System for Automatic Design of Printed Boards Taking INTO Account Requirements to Intra-Apparatus EMC
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Construction and possibilities of complex system of automatic design of printed boards are considered which allows to take into account requirements to intra-apparatus EMC in a single cycle of printed boards design. The system of automatic design is fulfilled using the technical means of the automized graphic complex on the basis of minicomputer CM-4 and is oriented on the standard operation system of real time with function separation. Information ensuring has a base system of design system issue and production of photomasks of printed boards and a subsystem ensuring the solution of problems of intra-apparatus EMC definition of electrical parameters of printed assemblage anu signal distortion in the printed unit. In the packages of applied programs used in the subsystem a problem-oriented dialog is used which allows to realize rational function distribution between the man and the machine. Calculation methods in the tasks of intra-apparatus EMC and structure of applied program package organization in the system of automatic design are described.

articleTitle: Spatial Shielding in Correlation to Resonances
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: In this paper a method of shield computation is presented, in which three basic shield models are taken to determine shield damping, also in the case of resonances. The method is not restricted solely to the centre of the room and is also applicable to shields of any lamination. Selected results are presented.

articleTitle: Solving Method of the Searle Coupled Equations and Their Application in the Sequency Theory
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: This paper presented first the Carry-Free Fast Walsh-Fourier Transform can be represented by the searle coupled equations, and gave one dependable solving method. these equations and their solving method are very useful in the sequency theory, such as not only can be applied logical network desing of the Carry-Free FWFT, but also quite adequate to demonstrate the detail transforming process and their important reversible properties etc. The importance of the searle coupled equations for digital communicat and signal processing are also briefly discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: The Past Synchronization in a Direct Sequence of Spread Spectrum Systems
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The time synchronization method in a direct sequence of spread spectrum systems for low signal-to-noise ratios and noncoherent reception is presented in this paper. Using the method, the synchronization time decreasing, in comparison to the other methods, has been assured. The method is based on a suitable choice of the crosscorrelation functions set, between both synchronization and reference signals. If a choice of such a set is done optimally, the mean synchronization time is in proportion to Ig<inf>2</inf>N/N-code length of signals/, but not to N like in the other methods.

articleTitle: Computer-Controlled High-Resolution Radio-Monitoring System
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: A high-resolution radio-monitoring system is formed of a suitable measuring receiver, an appropriate demodulator and a low-frequency FFT analyzer. The system measures field strengths and frequencies of signals with high selectivity. The FFT analyzer serves as a panoramic display and by computer evaluation of spectra the automatic identification and measurement of signals is possible. A brief overview of different measuring concepts is given. A simple approach is described to measure the magnitude of periodic signals.

articleTitle: The Influence of Helicopter Flight Parameters on the Results of Measurements of a Horizontal Radiation Patterns of VHF/UHF Broadcasting Antennae
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The selection of optimum flight parameters as well as navigation influence on the measurement results are discused. The corrections which permit a decrease in of measurement errors related to inaccuracte helicopter navigation are determined. An unconventional method of data processing was elaborated to increase the accuracy of determining the antenna pattern. The efficiency of the methods presented is illustrated with an example.

articleTitle: Plasmapause Guiding of VLF Transmissions as an Interference Source for the Sub-Ionospherically Propagated Signals
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Ariel 3 and 4 measurements of the GBR (16 kHz) and NAA (17.8 kHz) transmissions above the ionosphere occasionally revealed unusually high field strength in the conjugate hemisphere in the latitude range 50 to 70 deg., with a longitudinal extent which may, on one occasion, have exceeded 120 deg. The importance of this magnetospheric mode of propagation as a source of interference for sub-ionospheric signals from VLF transmitters is investigated.

articleTitle: Laboratory for the Measuring of the Industrial Interference
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: A laboratory for the electromagnetic compatibility was built in our Institute at 1985. This is a specially equipped laboratory used for the measuring of radio interference, simulation of the pulse interference and for the measurement of various devices as far as their resistance against interference is concerned. Devices are made by Rohde and Schwarz, Tektronix, Schaffner and Marconi. We can measure radio interference from 10 kHz to 1 GHz. The whole set of devices is exclusively oriented to the HP-IB bus, which enables us to measure fully automatically.

articleTitle: Transmission Line Antennas for Square Have Field Excitation
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Electronic: equipments and devices frequently are endangered by transient electromagnetic fields with rise times of a few ns and an electric peak fieldstrength of some 10 kV/m. For the testing of the susceptibility against such irradiated fields suited facilities with a defined field distribution such as transmission line antennas are used. It will be shown, that especially the geometrical design of the line feed resp. the line termination section affects decisively the rise time and also the time slope in the back of the traveling wave.

articleTitle: Closed form Solution for EMP Reflection by Earth
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: An exact solution for the transient reflected EM wave from a lossy earth is derived for the case of an obliquelly incident horizontally polarized impulsive plane wave. The obtained solution can be scaled in time and magnitude to cover responses of different kind of soil. The similar solutions are obtained for the case of an double exponential EMP. The solutions are expressed as an infinite serie of potential and exponential terms. Numerical results are presented for a variety of parameters to illustrate the possibilities of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: On the Antennas Without a Phase Centre and Their Applications
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: In the paper the concept of partial antennas and the definition of the common radiation centre for the case of antennas without a phase centre are introduced. On the basis of the above concept and definition, the formation of antennas with special phase patterns are considered, and the relations of antenna arrays constructed from the radiating elements without a phase centre are presented. Some applications of radiators with special phase patterns in antenna engineering are shown

articleTitle: A Study of Null Distribution of Nearfield of Aperture Antennae
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: SUMMARY: The knowledge of null distribution of nearfield of aperture antennae is important in environmental protection and avoidance of mutual coupling between adjacent antennae. Because of the difficulty in computation, the nearfield of an actual aperture antenna is obtained by measurements. In this paper we use the method of aperture partition and fast numerical method for Fresnel Integral evaluation for nearfield calculation. We calculate the nearfield infront of an 140λ offset paraboloid reflector to show the effectiveness of the method. Also, we compute the field distributions from 1D (140λ) to 4D, which have the following characteristics: 1) The power radiated is concentrated in a cylindrical volume infront of the antenna with a diameter a little bit larger than the aperture; 2) The field distribution is roughly the same as that of the field on the reflector; 3) The field outside the cylinder decays rapidly and is about -36dB below the peak. The deepest null is about -60dB; 4) There are fewer sidelobes than the farfield.

articleTitle: Reliability Tests for Telecom Equipment Against Surges
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: INTERFERENCE WITH EXCHANGE & SUBSCRIBERS EQUIPMENT DUE TO LINE DISTURBANCES - WORK OF CCITT STUDY GROUP V/RTIG The aims of CCITT Recommendations on telecom equipment reliability when exposed to line disturbances are explained. The sources of natural and man-made surges are described, and the use of simulated ciruits for surge tests is justified. The links between tests for reliability, EMC and electrical safety are outlined.

articleTitle: The Plasma Wave Environment of the Earth as Studied by the Ampte UKS Satellite Mission
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The AMPTE mission involved the use of three satellites to study, amongst other objectives, processes in the outer part of the earth's magnetosphere. Some results from the wave experiment on the UKS spacecraft are presented which are indicative of the plasma wave environment on the dayside of the earth's outer magnetosphere. These results are discussed in terms of both morphology and generation mechanisms.

articleTitle: Characteristics and Theory of Bypolar Flashes Observed from Rocket-Triggered Lightning Experiments
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Examinations of selected events of bipolar flashes observed from rocket-triggered lightning experiments in winter in a coastal region of the Sea of Japan reveals the following findings, based upon a new model: 1. A near-horizontal cloud shape and charge distribution is a configuration favourable for a bipolar flash. 2. A rocket with a grounded wire plays twofold roles in triggering a bipolar flash: one is an electric merging and the other is an artificial formation of an electric cusp. 3. Their boudary discontinuities lead to discharge triggering and EHD wind. 4. Discharge characteristics are well described in terms of an equivalent circuit.

articleTitle: Influence of Radio Transmitters Fundamental and Harmonics to Electronic Equipment
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Receivers of any type of radio services may be disturbed in their function by electromagnetic fields or currents. - Direct interference may be caused by harmonic content of the radio frequency signal (mostly fault of the transmitter). Disturbance or general impairment of operation could be caused by the fundamental r.-f. power of the transmitter (mostly fault of the disturbed device). This contribution shows the way of penetration and remedies by shielding, filtering and decoupling.

articleTitle: The Error for Open Field Radiated Measurements and its Discussion
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: This paper describes the problems in relation to error Signals, i.e., the classification, evaluation and reduction of the error due to unwanted signals. A unifying presentation is given for antenna and radiated emission measurements. This paper reviews some principal errors for the antenna and radiated emission measurements, it identifies the more significant errors, and offers an example of error budget of the antenna measurement. Finally, this paper reviews the problems in relation to radiated measurements at MMW frequencies.

articleTitle: Electrostatic Induction on Motor Vehicles Under Overhead Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: A technique and a computer program for calculating currents and voltages electrostatically induced on standard farm and road vehicles under high voltage overhead lines are described. The computation results are shown to be in a good agreement with the results of measurements made under operating lines. It is demonstrated that implementation of the USSR standard that limits electric fields under overhead lines to 10 kV/m on roads and to 15kV/m in non-residential areas ensures a safe level of electrostatic induction on vehicles.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model of Power Converter as a Source of High-Power Concentrated Interference
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Given are peculiarities of mathematical models of power converters as sources of high-power concentrated interference. Developed are methods of analysis, synthesis, and optimization of power converters of variable structures with the use of gate models of various degrees of complexity. The developed software for modeling converters allows to upgrade the electromagnetic compatibility between converters, information and power networks.

articleTitle: A Vertically Polarized Radar Antenna for Remote Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: A vertically polarized radar antenna is designed which consists of one hundred waveguide radiating elements. The radiating elements are located linearly, side by side, forming a line source of one hundred wavelengths in length and mounted inside a sectoral horn to shape its vertical radiation pattern. The unit was designed to provide low side lobes (less than 30 dB) in the horizontal plane and a beamwidth around one degree. In the vertical plane the antenna pattern was required to have sidelobe levels less than 2 dB and a beamwidth In excess of fifteen degrees. The unit was designed to be used as a remote sensing radar for investigation of ice formations in northern waters.

articleTitle: The EM Emission Phenomena as a Precursor of Earthquakes and the Possibility of Epicenter Location Prediction
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: This paper presents the observation results of electromagnetic emissions which appear before the first shock of earthquakes as the precursor, and include to examine the sourse mechanism of this phenomena. Also this paper shows one of the example of successful result of the earthquakes and its epicenter point prediction experiment by means of the multipoint direction finding networks which set up around Tokyo area since 1983.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Source and the Field in the Immediate Neighbourhood of Diffraction Wedge and its Application
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: An exact analysis for the diffraction characteristic of a metal wedge is carried out so that some constraints of the results in earlier papers are released. With the new formulas, we have analysed the azimuth pattern of the antenna array which has several stacks of longitudinal slots on the two broad walls of a rectangular waveguide. Theoretical results are compared with experimental ones.

articleTitle: Assessment of Levels of Radio Interference Produced by Vehicular Traffic
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The Report presents an analytical model of man-made radio interference (MMRI) produced by vehicular traffic. This model relates the parameters of electromagnetic environment at a reception point with the parameters of vehicular traffic and with the characteristics of MMRI produced by individual motor vehicles. As a characteristic of electromagnetic environment an average square of MMRI field strength is accepted. A case is discussed when a reception point is located outside of a motor-road, as well as a case when this reception point moves together with a vehicular traffic. A structure of vehicular traffic is taken into account and it is shown that its inhomogeneity has a great influence on the MMRI levels.

articleTitle: Some EMC Problems of Mine Wire Telecommunication Systems
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Improper operation of trolleyphone communication after introduction semiconductor rectifier stations as well as groundless electric energy breaks caused by CTT63/40U methanometric systems noticed the electromagnetic compatibility in depth coal mines. Research-Development Centre together with Silesian Technical University lead investigations on electromagnetic interference sources in mines and their influence on telecommunication systems. The results of investigations make the basis to develop the standards and regulations ensuring the electromagnetic compatibility of power networks and mine wire telecommunication systems.

articleTitle: Effect of Low Intensity Millimeter Wave Irradiation on UV-Light Indused Lysis of Yeast Cells
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Continious millimeter (MM, 6,0...8,5 mm) wave irradiation of yeast cells at the power density of order 10 mW/cm<inf>2</inf> was shown to increase the UV-induced release of substances with absorption maximum at 260 nm (nucleoproteides). No frequency dependence was observed. It is suggested that the acceleration of UV-lysis of yeast cells under MM irradiation is caused by the convective mixing of water medium facilitating photochemical and/or transport processes.

articleTitle: Tall Tower Triggered Lightning During Winter
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: To clarify the characteristics of tall tower triggered lightning, lightning currents have been measured by magnetic links and a digital recording system during winters at Niigata coast of Japan. The frequency of positive polarity flashes was higher than that of summer lightning. The bipolar strokes were recorded frequently in a lightning flash. The current waveforms of winter lightning were classified into eight types. Moreover, the winter lightning discharges were observed by still cameras and automatically driven video systems. The most flashes progress upward direction and the height of winter thunderclouds is very low.

articleTitle: Microwave Field Pattern Measurement for EMC Study
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The author has developed a robotic system for automatic measurement of a microwave field. An antenna (sensor) scans a field space to be measured. The data of each point in the scanned space is stored into memories and processed to display or print out as a field pattern. All systems are controlled by a microcomputer. Scattering field by an object to be studied can be obtained without use a special measuring site by obtaining a difference between the field intensity without object and that with object. Several measuring examples are presented such as a field pattern in a living space, diffraction pattern around the living body, pattern measurement of an effect of aprons for protection from microwave field, and so on.

articleTitle: The Chemistry of Intermodulation Interference and its Suppression
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Intermodulation interference (IMI) from non-linear metal-oxide-metal (MOM) junctions near HF and VHF transmitters and receivers can be suppressed effectively by removing the metal oxide and forming an alternate low reactance or low resistance current path between the metal structures. Chemicals were developed that perform these functions, reducing IMI below background levels in shipboard and land-based applications. The resulting "chemical ground straps" are environmentally stable, low cost, and effective over a wide spectral range.

articleTitle: Influence of External Low-Frequency Electromagnetic Field Upon a Biological Membrane in the Process of Transporting Ions
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The paper presents a biophysical model of the influence of external low-frequency electromagnetic fields upon the transport of ions through a biological membrane. Changes taking place in this transport produce changes in the accumulation of ions in the cells and tissues of a biological material being exposed to an electromagnetic field.

articleTitle: Some Deductions from the Travelling Current Source Model
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: In the "Travelling" Current Source"(TCS) model it is assumed that the charge of the downward leader, distributed in a vertical tube is discharged to earth by a fictive current source travelling along the lightning channel. From the sophisticated calculations of the shapes of the electric and magnetic field it is possible to derive simplified formulas with satisfying accuracy in results. By using these formulas the typical initial peak of the electric and magnetic field in LEMPs as well as the shape of the first derivation by time can be evaluated very easily.

articleTitle: Optimization of Radio Spectrum Use and Frequency Assignment Procedures for Mobile Radio Systems
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The paper presents a definition of spectral efficiency for mobile radio systems which includes the coverage strategy as a S.D.M.A. added to the other multiple access techniques envisaged for the system. The boundary conditions necessary for evaluating this parameter are carefully discussed. Several example are presented. The advantages obtainable by means of a field strength prediction method based on a geographical data base are shown.

articleTitle: Editing of Pulse Interferences in Digital Receiving Systems
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: A digital filter for editing of data in digital receiving systems is presented. It is intended for localizing and filtering of short time, wideband pulse interferences with a lifetime greater than the correlation interval of the received signal. One and the same signal is used for localizing of the interference as well as for its editing. Analytical expressions for the statistical parameters of the edited signal are obtained. It is shown that the filter has a high efficiency even without a priori information about the signal, and may operate in real time. An example is considered and a computer model of the filter is given.

articleTitle: The Application of Bridge Functions to Engineering
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: A bridge function system was introduced, where the bridge functions make up a three-valued system, only taking the values -1, 0, and +1, and connect the Walsh functions with block pulses. It can be proved that the bridge functions are orthogonal and complete when certain conditions are satisfied. In this paper, we try to develop the applications of the bridge functions to engineering.

articleTitle: Selective Interference in FM and TV Receivers
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The paper deals with the problem of selective interference caused by stations of the amateur radio service operating in the 2m, 70cm and 23cm bands to FM broadcast receivers and TV receivers. Sensitivity measurements of several BC and TV receivers at certain frequencies were carried out. However the measurements were made in the aspect of amateur radio service and with receivers of the OIRT standard, the obtained results and conclusions are valid also to other radio services and to frequency ranges of the CCIR standard respectively.

articleTitle: Electric Properties of the Uppermost Ground According to the Data of Airborne Probing
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The report considers the results of airborne probing of the uppermost ground in a very low frequency (VLF) range of radio waves. A regularity of electric properties change of the uppermost ground in the mountainous areas of a complicated geological structure has been ascertained. Quantitative characteristics for crystalline and sedimentary complexes of rocks have been found. Maps of effective resistance of the uppermost ground of the South Siberia have been made according to the results of measuring at frequencies 17,4 and 22,3 kHz.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility and Harmonic Distortion Measurement
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: For the investigation of the electromagnetic compatibility and limitation of interierences the knowledge of voltage and current harmonics has decesive importance. To measure harmonics we have built an automatic measuring workplace as a part of our Electromagnetic Compatibility Laboratory. Our measuring system is based on the application of the FFT frequency analyzers. Some harmonic measurement results are given.

articleTitle: Propagation and Radiation Behaviour of Rectangular Corrugated Feed with Slots Filled with Medium
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Hybrid modes in the rectangular corrugated horns with slots filled with medium are investigated, equations were developed for the hybrid mode fields which exist in the horns, propagation constants were obtained for the various modes of interest. A technique of combining several modes for pattern shaping is described. The mode amplitude ratio is calculated from a known throat excitation and used to compute radiation patterns. The theoretical patterns were in good agreement with experimental data. Finally, cross-polarized performance of the feed is investigated and the technique of double medium which is evenly filled in the corrugated slots is provided.

articleTitle: Reflecting Characteristics of Anisotropic Rubber Sheets and Measurement of Complex Permittivity Tensor
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: A rubber sheet manufactured by the rolling process shows a strong anisotropic property which is caused by carbon particles or carbon fibers aligned along the rolling direction. The measurement method of the complex permittivity tensor in the rubber sheet by the least squares method using the reflection loss measured for normal incidence is studied. The tensor including off-diagonal elements and the principal direction are measured and discussed. Errors in the measured tensor elements and principal direction are evaluated.

articleTitle: The Importance of Electromagnetic Compatibility for Modern Telecommunication Services
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: An overall review of current trends in the development of modern telecommunication services is given and their groving mutual interdependence is underlined. Particular attention is drawn to the fact, that the strong trend towards digitalisation and integration of telecommunication networks creates a lot of unexpected difficulties in the operation of such networks. The progress in the semiconductor technology and in the LSI and VLSI techniques makes the overcoming of these problems more and more difficult because of a lover level of signals being processed and a greater susceptibility of the integrated circuits to even not very strong electromagnetic fields. On the other hand, the advantages of fiber optic systems from the EMC point of view are presented.

articleTitle: Low Frequency Electromagnetic Fields and Biological Systems
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Experimental investigations in rats subjected to repeated exposure in e-m fields of 1 kHz, 10 kHz or 25 kHz and intensities ranging from 200 V/m to 3000 V/m have revealed retardation of animal growth rate and shifts of Na<inf>+</inf> and K<inf>+</inf> contents in some brain structures. These results indicate the difference of biological effects due to 1 kHz and 10 kHz e-m fields.

articleTitle: Modification of the Scattered Field of a Wire Scatterer by Impedance Loading
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The problem of modification of the scattered field of thin wire scatterers is studied. The problem is formulated analytically in terms of magnetic-potential-type integral equation for current distribution on the scatterer. The resulting formulas are in matrix notation (by means of the method of moments) in form suitable for programming on digital computers. Many numerical results for back scattering cross sections as a function of various geometry of wire and type of loads are included.

articleTitle: Decentralized Adaptive Organization of Radiostation Set Operation
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The report is concerned with the possibility of the introduction of autonomous adaptive choice of operation frequency (autochoice) in a set of uniform radiostations. The systems of frequency autochoice based on different principles are considered in literature. However, these systems are analised provided only one device works in the given electro-magnetic environment (EME). But this analysis is incomplete as it doesn't give information about the working capacity of the device set and the effectiveness of spectrum application. In fact, if there is no central station and every radiostation searches for radio-frequency according to local information in reception point without exchanging information with adjacent stations a number of problems arises due to undesired relations between the stations. First of all, it is a question of quiescent point existence in which the criterion of the frequency search by separate stations is held true. And at the same time it is a question of this point range (if it exists) in the process of autonomous frequency choice according to the conventional algorithm. In addition, the expediency of operation organization introduction from the point of view of the effective application of part of the spectrum selected for operation is of great interest. These problems' are considered in this report.

articleTitle: Monopulse Technique for an Array of Linear Wire Antennas
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The peak-amplitude and slope patterns of an array of linear wire antennas fed by a time-varying Gaussian pulse are obtained in the time domain, using a numerical method. The antennas are loaded with a nonlinear element in order to reduce the late-time response. The monopulse technique with the slope pattern is that promises a much better accuracy of angle measurement of a target.

articleTitle: Shielding of a Communication Data Link Against EMP Threat
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: A method is presented in this paper for determining the shielding effectiveness of metal shields to protect data links from EMP threats. For this purpose the EMP is expressed in double exponential analytical model. The cylindrical shielding structure is approximated by tubes made of steel, copper and aluminium seperately and is considered for working out mathematically the minimum thickness of tubular shields necessary for optimum shielding. The results of analysis are shown graphically. Computations are carried out using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) technique to get the EMP spectrum. Field coupling, into a metal tube, is evaluated using classical coupling equations.

articleTitle: EMC of the Terrestrial tv Broadcasting Service and the Fixed Service in the 12 GHZ Band
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The operation of various services in the frequency band between 11,7 GHz and 12,5 GHz as well as the sharing conditions in this band are regulated by the Table of frequency allocations and provisions 836 to 850 RR. Under the Radio Regulations this frequency bans is allocated, on a shared basis, to the broadcasting and fixed services. At the WARC-77 held in Geneva in 1977 only the sharing between the Broadcasting Satellite Service and terrestrial services in the 12 GHz band was considered. This report studies a problem of criteria development in the band 11, 7-12,5 GHz for the sharing between the broadcasting and fixed services. The difference between this problem and the solutions from a terrestrial transmitting TV station have somewhat peculiar characteristics compared with signals from a broadcasting satellite. The report formulates an approach to this problem aimed at the development of criteria which would ensure interierence-free sharing of the 12 GHzband by the services. The analysis presented in the report is based on CCIR texts.

articleTitle: Analysing the Properties of a Loop-Antenna System
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The objective of the study was to analyze the properties of a system incorporating three circular loop antennae (arranged perpendicular to each other) with coinciding centres. The data obtained in this study substantiate two particular uses of the system - as a probe of a spherical radiation characteristics for the measurement of the electromagnetic (EM) field, and as an indicator of the field structure. Probes having such properties may be achieved by applying system of appropriately loaded loop antennae, each of them being coupled to an active member with acts as a former-transformer unit for the voltages on the antenna loadings.

articleTitle: Relationship Between Night Airglow and Seimic Activity
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The results of photometric observations of night airglow at Abstumani Astrophysical Observatory overlapping with nearby earthquakes are given. The intensity increase of the green oxygen line (λ = 5577A °) during the night before an earthquake was found. Described phenomena may be related with an enhanced electron precipitation into ionosphere induced by radioemission of seismic origin.

articleTitle: C.A.D. of Waveguide Applicators for Microwave Hypertermia Applications
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: A direct contact type of hyperthermia applicators consisting of multi-stepped rectangular/square waveguides are accurately analyzed. The tissues are simulated by means of a multilayered configuration. Based on the analysis routine an optimization of geometry is maked in order to improve depth of penetration. Results confirm the usefulness of these applicators.

articleTitle: State Variables Sensitivity in Power Inverter Circuits to Predetermined Influences
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Considered are sensitivity functions to state variables in power inverters which are sources of high-power concentrated interference. Predetermined influences are represented by parameters of sets of differential equations with discontinuous right sides. Investigated is differentiability of these equations by initial values and parameters. An objective functional is represented in the Mayer form.

articleTitle: Electrical Equipment as Sources of Radio Interferences in Ships Power Lines
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The paper deals with the investigation results of disturbances generated by ship's electrical appliances in the frequency band 10 kHz to 30 MHz. There have been presented the main sources of disturbances localized in synchronous generators, excitation and regulation voltage systems, thyristor systems of phase control, converters and the main electrical drive systems.

articleTitle: EMC Systems Engineering for the Ampte UKS Satellite
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The AMPTE-UKS spacecraft [1] was designed as a low cost research satellite produced in a remarkably short time (three years from approval to launch) but to a high specification for performance in orbit. The purpose of this paper is to discuss the EMC problems which were identified early in the project and present both the EMC solutions which were adopted and the test plan developed for verification. Some results from the test programme are presented together with a discussion of the performance achieved in orbit.

articleTitle: State of EMC Standardization in Czechoslovakia
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The complicated problems of EMC arising from increasing utilization of electronic power control and other sources of interference, caused an urgent need to limit dangerous and disturbing effects from interference sources upon broadcast reception, power supply networks, control systems etc, as well as to raise noise immunity of possible interference receiverse Based on several well established international and national documents several new national and departmental standards have been produced in Czechoslovakia recently. The paper presents a survey of these.

articleTitle: Some Investigation of New Type Transient Protective Devices
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Methodology and experimental results of protective properties of the monocrystallic silicon at T = 4,2° K are presented. In this paper the structure of tested samples, oscillograph records of the silicon sample breakdown voltage and its dynamic voltage-current characteristics are shown. Erom these experiments it is evidence that the silicon in cryogenic temperature may be advantageous for construction of the protective elements in radio-electronic engineering equipments and systems, to protect against fast transients and lightning overvoltages.

articleTitle: Analysis of Complex Protecting Devices by Means of Quadripole Theory
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The contribution deals with the analysis and synthesis of circuits for the protection of wire telecommunication equipment against transient overvoltages. Based on the quadripole theory a method is presented, which allows to compose complex protecting cascades using simple basic quadripole elements. Further on it is shown how to apply the known calculation methods of the quadripole theory to such protecting networks. Doing so, a simple method is dealt with which makes it possible to analyse the non-linear voltage limiting behaviour.

articleTitle: Field Radiated by Cloud-Ground Lightning Above a Finitely Conducting Soil. Study of the Domains of Validity of the Different Approximations of Sommerfeld Integrals. Elaboration of an Efficient Numerical Code
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: In order to compute the electromagnetic radiation of a return-stroke in a lightning flash in the case of a dissipative half-space, it is necessary to evaluate the Sommerfeld integrals, present in the field equation of a dipole electric. To reduce the computation time, these integrals have been calculated, considering different approximations available in the technical literature and the domain of validity of each of them is presented.

articleTitle: Two Level Simulation for the Evaluation of Frequency Assignment Strategies
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: In the paper a two level simulation algorithm is described, by which an effective computer-aided frequency assigment method can be developed for temporarily deployed radio systems, which are organized in a hierarchical structure. The first level of the simulation is for evaluating the spectrum utilization of the candidate assigment methods, while the second one is a complete EMC analysis. The simulation was run for two strategies, which were found as the potentially best ones according to other publications.

articleTitle: Conductive Coatings for EMI/RFI Shielding
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: When most communication and business machine equipment was housed in metal enclosures, the problems of electro-magnetic (EMI) and radiofrequency (RFI) interference were slight. The increasing use of engineered plastics has now focused greater attention on methods of preventing EMI/RFI and in this area conductive coatings have a major role to play.

articleTitle: Shielding Effectivenes of Conductive Wires Over the Underground Railway Lines
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Magnetic fields caused by currents in underground railway lines may cause interference in operation of electronic equipments or systems which are working in building near or over these railway lines. In this paper analysis one of the shielding method is presented. In this method the additional copper or steel wire were put over the railway line. These wires are insulated or connected with railway rail and in these wires the current flow in contrary to that of the contact system.

articleTitle: Tests to be Carried Out on Transitorized Long Distance Transmission Equipment to Check the Efficiency of Protection from External Interferences According to CCITT Recommendations
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Question 21/V of CCITT is concerned with protection of long distance transmission equipment from external electromagnetic interference. Up to now three Recommendations were published which describe principles for protection measures as well as specification for testing procedures in full detail. Test procedures recommended by CCITT with regard to power line induction and lightning interferences proved to be reliable and satisfactory in the past. The wide spread use of digital equipment in the future may entail recommendations with regard to interference sources other than ac-induction and lightning.

articleTitle: Radiorefractivity and Refractivity Effects in the Coastal Zone of Northern Poland
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Basing on many years statistical data, investigations of the radiorefractive index in the 100 m thick ground layer of the troposphere in the coastal zone of Northern Poland had been carried out. The influence of the annual cycle was examined. Furthermore, an attempt had been undertaken to prove the effect of the variability of the radiorefractive gradient on coverage conditions in the above mentioned area. The results of the study show that the greatest variability of propagation conditions should be expected in the summer season.

articleTitle: Characteristics of BMI Statistical Parameters APD and NAD and Their Measurements
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Use of the statistical parameters APD and NAD to study electromagnetic interference is discussed. The design concepts, construction, details, and performance of the first Chinese APD/NAD measurement instrument are described. The instrument consists of medium scale integrated circuits and is controlled by a Chinese TP801-Z80 microprocessor. Using computer software instead of hardware. simplifies the circuitry of the instrument. The results of the measurements of the ignition noise of a Chinese Model 130 truck and the noise of an electric railway u9ing this instrument are analyzed and their APD and NAD data are plotted. The curves show the probability distributions and the main pulse rates of the noises.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Efficient Incoherent Analogue Modulation Methods
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: A review is described of incoherent analogue modulation methods that make full use of channel bandwidth. This is achieved either by employing one modulation parameter only, or using simultaneous amplitude and frequency modulation. Modulation methods belonging to both groups are described and compared, and their performances and implementation techniques are discussed.

articleTitle: Conductive Interference of Short - Circuit Current Flowing Through A H.V. Station Earth Electrode on Nearby Conductors with Earth Return
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: In the event of an earth fault occuring at a h.v. station the nearby buried conductors may be exposed to conductive effects of the earth-fault current flowing to the earth through a h.v. earth electrode. In the paper by specializing the driving electric field calculations are made and formulas derived, applicable to the analysis of potentials excited by the conductive effect, along two infinitely long conductors with earth return, buried in the vicinity of a h.v. station earthing, which is assumed to be a round plate electrode. The technical application of the method presented is illustrated by an example.

Author Keywords: Conductive interference - Earth return circuit - Earthing

articleTitle: Microwave Absorbing Materials of Metal-Fiber Mixed Ferrite-Resin Composite
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
