abstract: In order to modify the dielectric properties of ferrite-resin composite material, short metal fibers are mixed with the material. The fiber mixed material permittivity shows artificial dielectric properties, which include resonance due to 1/2 wave length in ferrite resin medium. An ultra broad-band absorber could be developed (e.g. more than 15 db absorption between 8 GHz and 26 GHz) both below and above the resonance regions, while a broad-band absorber was achieved in the below resonance region (e.g. typically more than 20 db absorption over 4.5 GHz in the X-band).

articleTitle: Signal Analysis by a Subclass of Hadamard Matrix
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The subclass of Hadamard matrix has been proposed in this paper. It is shown that a class of discrete digital signal can be represented with the spectral points of subclass of Hadamard matrix. By permutation, The Walsh-Hadamard transform can be used to carry out the signal's pseudo-randomization.

articleTitle: Unshielded Simple Cable Configurations Illuminated by Lightning Electromagnetic Pulses
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: A direct lightning stroke to a building may cause damages or interferences in operation of majority of electronic and electric systems. For this reason in this paper an attempt has been made to determine theoretically the voltages induced in low-voltage unshielded simple cables situated in the interiority of buildings struck by lightnings. The calculations of these voltages were carried out by changing dimensions of the cable configuration and their places in respect to the stricking point.

articleTitle: A New Four-Wire Transmission Circuit with Suppression of Magnetic Induced Interfering Voltages
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Inductively coupled-in interfering voltages can be compensated to a large extend by using a new four-wire transmission circuit. The circuit uses concentric geometry for better compensation of nearby interference sources. For economic realization the receiving (compensating and terminating) network can be passive. The properties of the circuit are discussed in detail. Practical results confirm the theoretical considerations.

articleTitle: CCITT Directives. The Volume on the Theory of Electromagnetic Coupling and the Basic Calculation Methods
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: After a very short overview on the organization of the new CCITT Directives in the form of different volumes, the content of the volume on the theory of electromagnetic coupling and the basic calculation methods is described. Special attention is paid on the calculation methods based on the multiconductor line theory.

articleTitle: Radio Signals Mutual Relations Index
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The known signal's relations coefficients such as mutual resolution coefficient, compatibility coefficient, probability of successful communication and so on have been shortly discussed and compared. Then the new measure called the signal distance index has been introduced. It is expressed, in the simplest case, by the probability that the value of a given signal feature / e.g. envelope level / exceeds the appropriate value of interference. Some examples of application of the new measure have been done.

articleTitle: Systematic Analysis of Interference of Fading Radio Signals
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Investigation of fading radio signals is reported. Three probabilistic signal models /by Rayleigh, Rice and Nakagami/ and their combinations are analyzed. Two novel results have been published recently by these authors. The paper presents four novel closed-form expressions for the interference probability, with Rician signals included. All 6 results are general, exact and surprisingly simple. Merits of the Nakagami model are emphasized.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Influence of the Mode Type on Microstrip Antenna Directive Properties
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The subject of this paper is the analysis of the mode type influence on the directive properties of a microstrip antenna with a rectangular radiating element-Investigations in this field were carried out using the aperture model of the antenna-The results of numerical investigations are presented.

articleTitle: Space-Time and Spectrum Distributions of Extremely Low Frequency Radionoise in the Middle Latitudes of the East of the USSR
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Results of experimental investigation of the natural electromagnetic Earth field in the band 5-200 Hz (ELF noise) which was carried out in the middle latitudes of the East of the USSR are summarised. An expeditionary high sensitivity receiving equipment for synchronous recording and processing of horizontal ELF noise components E<inf>h</inf> and H<inf>h</inf> at the earth surface is described. Basic regularities of space-time and spectrum distributions of the ELF noise intensity have been ascertained for central Asia, distant from the world thunderstorm activity centers. A structure of the global resonances of the Earth-ionosphere cavity has been considered. Effects of solar eclipse on July 31, 1981 are discussed. An ELF noise application for the electromagnetic depth sounding of the Earth crust has been considered.

articleTitle: Lightning Surge Waves Induced on Overhead and Buried Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Disturbing currents may be induced on the outer shield of overhead buried telecommunications cables by lightning strokes. In this paper a model of lightning discharges is used to determine the response of the line. Using a transmission line theory we first give the current distribution in frequency and time domain. A comparison with experimental results obtained at St Privat d'Allier in 1983 is also given.

articleTitle: Investigation of Voltages Induced on Cable Lines and Electronic Equipment Under HV Substation Conditions
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Measurement and calculation results of induced voltages at Class 500 and 220 kv substations under different operational conditions are presented. The main source of interferences when using even poor screened communication cables is pulse potential resulting from switching action in power supply network and measuring circuit grounding points. Interference level at short-circuits is lower than that at switching action. Power supply network protection grounding points optimisation and potential leveling, isolation transformer and blocking inductive coil installation, circuit balancing are recommended.

articleTitle: Calculation of Attenuation for Waveguide Below Cut off as a Vent Hole in Enclosure
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The effects of seams, cracks, openings, holes and other breaks in a shield can be developed by considering the opening as a waveguide below cut off (WBCO) and determing the waveguide attenuation. Based on equivalent transmission line method, this paper deals with the general formula of attenuation for waveguide below cut off, and gives simple analytical formula of attenuation for circular/rectangular waveguide with H<inf>11</inf>,E<inf>11</inf>/ H<inf>11</inf> mode. In addition to this, baseo on requirements associated with electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), the shield performances of electronic equipment configuration in relation to some factors of influence are described in this paper. Also, it offers specific recommentation on the positions related to leakage of electromagnetic energy.

articleTitle: An Auto-Tracking Parabolic Sensing Antenna with Dual Mode Archimedian Spiral Feed
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: In this paper, an intorduction of an auto-tracking parabolic sensing antenna with dual mode archimedian spiral feed is given. Theiretical analysis, calculation and experiment have also been made. The theoretical values tally with the measured values. The results show that this antenna is suitable for remote sensing. The key to obtain the excellent performances is the good balanced performance ofΣ|,Δ| networks, the geometry symmetry of the antenna and the feed, the high polarization purity, and the satisfactory phase patterns.

articleTitle: The Occurence of Overvoltages and Overcurrents on Telecommunication Lines
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: An economically based overvoltage protection system must take into account the probability of occurrence of overvoltages on telecommunication lines and their parameters. In the P.&T. Research Institute in Prague measurements have been carried out to get the basic data on overvoltage parameters. To enable a more generalized view on overvoltage and overcurrent parameters, the results of overvoltage measurements published in twelve other papers were analysed. In conclusion, the utilization of the results of analysis in solving protection problems are discussed.

articleTitle: Primary Mechanisms of MM Wave Biological Effects Caused by Strong Microwave Absorption of Water
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Continuous millimeter (MM) wave irradiation of water solutions in cuvettes leads to:i)interface convection due to surface tension gradients; ii) decrease in melting temperature of liposomes from dipalmitoyllecythin; iii) acceleration of H<inf>+</inf> transfer from water to pyridine molecules. These effects are caused "by strong bsorp on of MM wave energy by water molecules, and may be responsible for the biological effects of low intensity MM wave irradiation.

articleTitle: On the Wire Configuration Study in the Time Domain
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Complex wire configurations excited by pulsed electromagnetic signals are analysed in the time domain, using the integral equation of the electric field (EFIE). This equation is transformed into a suitable expression to calculate, by numerical computation, the current distribution on the wire structure.

articleTitle: Compatibility Criteria Between Television Signal and Spread-Spectrum Signals
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The paper deals with the possibility of coexistence of a spread-spectrum system sharing the same frequency band, on mutual noninterference basis, with a television transmitter. Frequency-hopping and direct-sequence techniques are examined, and the required protection ratios for providing an imperceptible television quality degradation are experimentally derived by means of subjective assessment tests.

articleTitle: The Disturbances Produced in a Typical Household Equipment and the in Influence on a Radio Receiver with a Ferrite Antenna
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: In this paper the results of measurements interference generated by a typical household equipment are presented. The character these interferences the contents of the symmetrical and asymmetrical components is determined. The procedure of measurement and measuring position to simulation of an interaction of an actual source of disturbance on a radio receiver with a ferrite antenna is worked out. The analysis of a penetration interference with a power network in a radio receiver with a ferrite antenna for a symmetrical and asymmetrical interferences is achieved. The veryfication of an obtained analytic results is made. The obtained effects are commented with critical attitude to protection of quality radio reception.

articleTitle: Noise Voltage Induced from Inside Power Lines Affecting Telecommunication Inside Wires
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: This paper describes the noise voltage characteristics induced from a power line affecting an inside wire. The continuous noise voltage is estimated using a new coupling coefficient evaluation method and CISPR's recommendation. Transient noise voltage measurements are carried out on a lot of electric apparatuses. Transient noise voltage is found to be much larger than continuous one. The twisted inside wire is quantitatively clarified to be useful for the transmission of digital signals from the view point of noise.

articleTitle: A Method of Producing Random Pulse Signals
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The paper presents a method of using microcomputer and single hoard computer to produce random pulses whose amplitude and separation interval can very in accordance with the definite statistical distributions. The random pulses can be used to simulate some radio noises. The random pulse generator is described in detail.

articleTitle: The Correlative Feature and Logical Network Design of the Modulo 2n Valued Operations
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: This paper discusses the correlative feature between modulo 2<inf>n</inf> valued additions ⊕<sub>2</sub> and subtractions ⊖<sub>2</sub>-operation first suggests their intricate truth table and the logical EXCLUSIVE-or conversions, and by using an analytic method of the Boolean logic presents a series general formulas of the ⊕<sub>2</sub> and ⊖<sub>2</sub> operations etc. A logical network design for the modulo 2<inf>n</inf> valued operations is worked out, which facilitates application of these operations in the information transmission and the number communication etc. The importance of the modulo 2<inf>n</inf> valued operations in time of n>2,and the future expectations of their application are also discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Improving the Accuracy of Measurement of VHF/UHF Broadcasting Antenna Radiation Patterns by Means of Filtration
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: The directional properties of typical television antenna systems in the horizontal plane have been analysed. The analysis showed that. an improvement of measurement accuracy may be achieved by means of Fourier's series approximation, taking the first 12 terms into account. The results obtained for a UHF antenna with and without the use of filtration have been compared. The comparison proves that filtration diminishes measurement errors while slightly influencing the irregularity of the antenna pattern.

articleTitle: Microstrip Disk Applicators for Biomedical Applications: A Very Efficient Numerical Analysis Technique
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: A microstrip disk applicator strongly coupled to a lossy medium facing the antenna is considered: the evaluation of the e.m. characteristics is obtained by an accurate analysis and a numerical approach, based on the equivalence principle and on the method of moments respectively. The efficiency of the antenna and its capability to perform a fixed radiation pattern in multi-frequency conditions are evaluated drawing the power density pattern in the biological medium.

articleTitle: Prony's Method Applied to Processing Electromagnetic Transient Data
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: In this paper we compare the results obtained using different autoregresive (AR) parameter estimation algorithms at the pole estimation block of the extended Prony method. The method is applied to the extraction of the poles and residues of the backscattered field for a Gaussian pulse incident from some different angles on a straight wire. Numerical examples for several cases are presented.

articleTitle: Experimental Evidence of VLF Discrete Emissions and Earthquakes Relationship
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Experimental data confirming the possibility of electromagnetic emission generation in the Earth’s crust as result of the earthquake preparedness are presented. The compared seismological data and those about the intensity of the natural very lowfrequency electromagnetic emission at two fixed frequencies - 5 and 9 kHz show that the level of the natural radionoise increases a few hours before a given earthquake. The possibility to use the intensity variation of the natural electromagnetic emissions as an operative precursor of impeding seismic events is discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis and Simulation of Transient E-Field Coupling to Cables and Circuits
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: In this paper, an analysis is made to estimate the coupling of transient E-field to interconnecting cables and circuits. The frequency spectrum of a known transient waveform from a transient generator is computed using 64 point Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and E-field coupling to cable and circuits is then calculated. The Inverse Discrete Fourier Transform (ID FT) is then calculated which gives the time domain waveform of the coupled transient at the output. A parallel plate antenna built in the laboratory is used for generating the transient E-field. The combined cable and circuit models built for the purpose are subjected to thus generated E-field and the output waveforms are graphically presented.

articleTitle: Microwave Propagation in Semi-Desert Conditions
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: In this paper results of observations made on a terrestrial microwave link operating in the Khartoum region are revealed. The paper addresses two aspects of microwave propagation in semi-desert regions; these are: (i) Attenuation effect of dust storms, and (ii) Multipath propagation due to surface ducts. It is found that attenuation due to dust storms is negligable. On the other hand multipath propagation was observed to occur frequently between sun set and sun rise. It is also found that evenings of hot days are more susceptable to surface duct formation and therefore multipath propagation.

articleTitle: EM Environment and LF Radiation in Outer Ionosphere
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: According to a complex experiment aided by "Interkosmos 19" satellite, simultaneous investigations of components of LF field and plasma were conducted which purpose was to clarify the propagation conditions of LF waves in the upper ionosphere at medium latitudes. The hypothesis from[6] about the possibility of LF radiation excitation at high concentration pradiente was proved. It was stated that at medium latitudes (≤50°) on all frequencies of ELF range, the waves propagate quasi-longitudinally, i.e. LF waves, appearing in the equatorial region at the plasmasphere height, propagate practically along the force lines of the magnetic field. In the quiet and moderately disturbed conditions and at the lack of concentration measurements, one may use at medium latitudes simultaneous measurmenets of magnetic and electric components of the LF field. A 10 to 15% accuracy of coincidence of theoretical and experimental values of plasma particle concentration at the satellite height, makes it possible to use the results of the satellite experiments in determining plasma parameters.

articleTitle: A Critical Examination of Geometrical Optics Solutions of High Frequency Solutions to Open and Closed Shell Problems
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Use is made of the Green's function of a line electric source inside a closed dielectric circularly cylindrical shell, to investigate the range for the valid use of G.O. ray soultion of the field. The possible simplification by the use of composite transmission/refelction coefficients is shown. Accuracy of the various approximations is shown by reference to a 90 term eigenfunction series summation.

articleTitle: On High Spectral Efficiency Coding of Frequency-Hopped Channels
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: Signature coding problem for multiple user communication systems is formulated. Signature codes for a frequency-hopped channel are presented. It is shown how to use signature codes to get high spectral efficiency in the frequency-hopped system.

articleTitle: A Survey of Radiofrequency and Microwave Electromagnetic Radiation Exposure Limits Suggested Guidelines for Italian Regulation
publicationTitle: Eight International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility 1986
abstract: To protect the general population and occupationally exposed individuals by RFR exposure risks. in various countries, protection and safety standards have been promulgated to limit the amount and the time of exposure which. individual scan receive without sustaining any injuries. Safe exposure limits, as proposed in various countries. differ from each other greatly owing to many uncertainties about RFR interaction mechanisms with biological systems. This paper aims to point out the main trends, philosophy and various concepts of standard setting, while drowing a survey of requirements of safety standards in Western and eastern Countries. The emphasis is on the latest international trends on the development and establishing of the electromagnetic radiation protection standards. Finally this paper aims to illustrate standards and guidelines as proposed for Italian regulation.
